entries.claim: FORMAT.md lines 28 and 42 say the seven brief sections and the five PRD sections are 'written in this order', but checkNamed only checks that each section is present, appears once and isn't empty. It never checks their order, so a misordered brief or PRD passes. checkEpic does enforce order for the equivalent epic-field rule, so the two rules are treated differently.
entries.failure_scenario: Copy samples/ and move '## Solution' with its body above '## Problem' in brief.md, or move '## MVP scope' above '## Requirements' in prd.md. checkDir returns [], and `node lib/check.mjs <copy>` exits 0 and prints 'seldon check: all four documents conform' (I ran both probes against the real module). Any /seldon output with its sections reordered would pass the gate, even though FORMAT.md says the check enforces the documented format and covers 'what this document defines'.

entries.claim: parse() strips trailing whitespace from every '## ' heading (line.slice(3).trimEnd()) before comparing it to the section names. FORMAT.md line 24 says section names are 'matched exactly', so the check accepts headings that an exact-match reader built from FORMAT.md would not recognize.
entries.failure_scenario: In a copy of samples/brief.md, change '## Vision' to '## Vision   ' (or end it with a tab). checkDir returns [] and the CLI exits 0 (I ran this probe). A Cadence reader that follows FORMAT.md literally takes the heading name as the rest of the line, gets 'Vision   ', and doesn't find the required Vision section in a document the check accepted. The same applies to every brief and PRD heading.
